clue.text: Part of France's established church

parts.note: something established has been shown to be true, i.e. proven
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A remark about the official state church of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France's established church' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'France'; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Provence is a region in the south-east of the country, on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Splendid, if cheap, shot by Yankee

indicators.note: the Yankee sits beside the rearranged letters
a shot item is ruined or broken, so the letters of cheap are rearranged

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American's cheap shot is grudgingly admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheap shot' reads as a phrase; 'shot' signals the anagram of CHEAP as PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is informal for excellent or fine, a synonym of splendid.

clue.text: Officer not content, having criticised a bloomer

indicators.note: the content of officer, its inside, is dropped, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to criticise

explanation.surface: An unhappy officer has scolded someone for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' in the surface is a British word for a blunder; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Procedure for rejecting an antique settee left uncovered outside

indicators.note: the uncovered settee sits outside, round the reduced antique
the settee's covering, its first and last letters, is removed
the word an is rejected, taken out of antique

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for turning down an old sofa left bare outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The uncovered settee goes round the trimmed antique, splitting after its first letter E. The surface's 'left' suggests L but belongs to the indicator 'left uncovered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the accepted code of correct behaviour, the proper form or protocol.

clue.text: Open space on riverside for financial institution

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a clearing is an open space in a wood
a bank is the side of a river

explanation.surface: A bank opening a branch in a glade by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearing bank is a British high-street bank that settles cheques through a clearing house.

clue.text: Rereading Proust produces a state of mental inertia

indicators.note: reading the letters again in a new order, so the name Proust is rearranged

explanation.surface: Going back over Proust's long novel leaves the reader numb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rereading' signals the anagram of PROUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed condition in which the mind barely functions.

clue.text: Letter from abroad for volunteer soldiers until recently

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet
..., the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve until renamed the Army Reserve in 2014

explanation.surface: A letter posted overseas to part-time soldiers in former days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from abroad' is a foreign alphabet letter, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet; the TA was the old reserve force.

clue.text: Mediterranean city's temper is rising. Help!

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word goes upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a strop is a bad temper
aid means help

explanation.surface: Tempers in a Mediterranean city are flaring, prompting a cry for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses STROP, a British word for a sulk, to PORTS; 'is' is a link from city's.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is an Egyptian city at the northern end of the Suez Canal.

clue.text: Our steel is forged to be firm

indicators.note: forging hammers metal into a new form, so the letters of our steel are reshaped

explanation.surface: A boast that the national steel is made to be strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means determined and unwavering, holding firm.

clue.text: Cashier lost about five records

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the five, enclosing it
letters that are lost wander out of place, so the word cashier is rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A bank clerk has mislaid roughly five documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges CASHIER as ARCHIES, and 'about' wraps that round V.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents and records kept for reference.

clue.text: These are black and white underwear items on non-binary third person

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another is written after it

parts.note: ze is a gender-neutral third-person pronoun
bras are items of underwear

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of monochrome lingerie worn by a non-binary person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ze' is a gender-neutral pronoun some people use instead of he or she.
explanation.definitionFit: Zebras are striped animals whose coats are famously black and white.

clue.text: Everything for Montgomery?

definitions.meaning: ... is an idiom for everything, the whole lot

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading turns the idiom literal: the full version of the name Monty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the complete set; Montgomery is the unabbreviated form of the nickname.

clue.text: This country is back — after having an illness — that's just for starters

indicators.note: the reversed country comes after the initials in the answer
only the starting letter of each of the three words having, an, illness is used
the country is written back to front

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Someone home again after being ill, offering a small first course of words.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself has five, seven and five syllables, so 'This' points at the clue as an example; some read the whole clue as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is a three-line Japanese verse form with lines of five, seven and five syllables.

clue.text: Try to be seen in reflected light for practice

indicators.note: the try appears within the reversed light, placed inside it
a reflection turns the word back, so laser is read backwards

parts.note: a laser is a beam of light
to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: An attempt to be visible in bounced light, as a training exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like a verb of effort; in court a judge hears, or tries, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice performance before the real one.

clue.text: Rogue nation, if kept under threat

indicators.note: a rogue strays from good order, so the letters of nation, if, kept are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rogue state, if detained, would be placed under menace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like an adjective for 'nation' but signals the anagram of NATIONIFKEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held at knifepoint means being menaced with a blade, an extreme kind of threat.

clue.text: Sexism may be regularly sparked by vodka essence in non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the regular letters sit beside the rest
every other letter of sparked is taken at regular intervals
the vodka essence goes inside the drink

parts.note: juice is a soft drink

indicators.note: the essence of vodka is its central letter

explanation.surface: Bias flares up at the bar when a teetotal drink is spiked with vodka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives PRE from sParKeD; 'essence' gives D, the middle of VODKA, placed 'in' JUICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexism is an example of bias, an unfair preconceived judgement against a group.

clue.text: Endorsement of commercial choice

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Backing for a choice made on commercial grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a policy means formally accepting or approving it.

clue.text: Supporter for the woman in a depression

indicators.note: the woman goes inside a depression

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A fan helping a woman through low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood; here it is a hollow, DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a cause or leader.

clue.text: Matador does this extremely elegant manoeuvre to avoid disaster

parts.note: a matador sidesteps the charging animal, i.e. dodges a bull

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, the outermost ones, of elegant are used

explanation.surface: A bullfighter's graceful sidestep keeps catastrophe at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives ET, the outer letters of 'elegant'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge a bullet is an idiom for narrowly escaping trouble or harm.

clue.text: Stretch and have a long life, it is said

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, so the answer matches what is heard

parts.note: to die late is to have a long life

explanation.surface: A wish to extend oneself and live to a great age.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or expand, as pupils do.

clue.text: Reckless to ignore Malaysia's capital for a break

indicators.note: the capital is ignored, left out of reckless

parts.note: KL is the usual abbreviation for Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia's capital

explanation.surface: A careless traveller skips Kuala Lumpur on a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a capital letter M, but it is the whole city, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or break, as in a school or parliament.

clue.text: Note Europe's backing Philistine's approval of Matilda?

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter
EU is the European Union

indicators.note: the setter's approval goes backwards, read in reverse

parts.note: Philistine is the setter, so his approval is my nod

explanation.surface: A setter jotting a note about Europe and endorsing someone called Matilda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses MY NOD, the setter's own nod, to DONYM. Matilda is another Guardian setter's alias, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Matilda is an example of a pen name, the name a crossword setter publishes under.

clue.text: Stop rejecting the heart of Jesus to become a believer

indicators.note: the heart letter is rejected, removed from the word for stop

parts.note: desist means stop

indicators.note: the central letter of Jesus is taken

explanation.surface: A sceptic gives up turning away from Christ and finds faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart of' gives S, the middle of JESUS, which 'rejecting' removes from DESIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A deist believes in a creator god but not in revelation.

clue.text: Join university before half-term

indicators.note: the university comes before the half-term in the answer
only the first half of the word term is used

explanation.surface: Signing up to a university just before a mid-term holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-term' looks like a school break but means TE, half of 'term'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring or come together, joining as one.

clue.text: Spain and Portugal start to indict secret police chief

indicators.note: only the starting letter of indict is used

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD

explanation.surface: Two countries begin proceedings against a head of state security.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian Peninsula is the landmass shared by those two countries.

clue.text: Jazz fan appearing in different music show

indicators.note: the jazz fan shows up inside the music, placed within it

parts.note: indie is alternative music, different from the mainstream
a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A jazz lover turns up in an unusual musical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music show' looks like one phrase, but 'show' is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or make plain, a synonym of show.

clue.text: One reason to visit the National Gallery would be to write music!

parts.words: One reason to visit the National Gallery would be
parts.note: a joke about London's two big galleries: if the other famous one were missing, you would go to the National

explanation.surface: A gallery-goer's justification turns into a musical composition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'no Tate': with no Tate gallery to visit, one goes to the National instead. Both are London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set down music in written symbols on the stave.

clue.text: Fire, having caught sight of retreat in range

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of burning material, a fire

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the sighting is read backwards

parts.note: seen means caught sight of

explanation.surface: A blaze spotted while withdrawing through hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reverses SEEN to NEES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the mountain range between France and Spain.
